title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. A generative video tool was used to produce footage of a real candidate saying words she never said, and the output was published on a sitting congressman's account. The false statements were placed in the mouth of a named person, which is the defining feature of a deepfake rather than a generic synthetic clip. The deployment context is political advertising, where the audience has no independent way to verify whether a candidate actually spoke.

The failure sits at the point of publication, not at the point of generation. A tool that renders a person's likeness will render whatever it is asked to render, so the check that matters is a human one before posting. Catching this would have required the account holder or a staffer to confirm that the depicted speaker had in fact said the words, which the reporting indicates she had not. Nothing in the facts shows a technical safeguard failing, because none is described as having been in place.

The videos were labelled as made with Grok Imagine, so the synthetic origin was disclosed even as the statements were presented as real. The cease-and-desist letter is an allegation by Cooke's attorneys, not a finding by a court, and no ruling on defamation has been established. Whether the videos were intended to deceive, and whether any legal consequence will follow, is not established by the reporting.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over AI-generated videos posted to his X account. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. The videos, labeled as made with Grok Imagine, show a fake Cooke saying things she never said, including a claim about corruption and free healthcare for undocumented immigrants. The letter, dated Sept. 30, calls the content pure fiction and says Van Orden could face defamation claims under state law.

Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum, and he responded with another AI video featuring a duck saying cease and desist. Cooke's attorneys say they are monitoring his accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Cooke first ran for the seat in 2022, lost the primary, won the Democratic primary in 2024, and lost the general election to Van Orden by about 3 percentage points.
